title: Mount drivers: MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET is read when the handler runs, so a GoTo admitted before a mode change becomes a sync
description: Found on 2026-11-21 while investigating ticket c3aeb19f-08e7-4d4b-a897-d9cf2002d6cf; reproduced in the mount_simulator and mount_synscan simulator suites with scratch cases. MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET has no BUSY guard (indigo_mount_driver.c about lines 696-700) and the queued coordinates handler reads the mode when it runs, not at admission: if SYNC is selected after a GoTo is admitted but before its handler runs, the handler syncs to the GoTo target, publishes OK at once and the mount never moves. In mount_synscan the GoTo finalizer also reads MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET_TRACK_ITEM at the end of the slew (indigo_mount_synscan.driver about line 1818), so a 'slew and track' GoTo can end with tracking off when the mode was changed meanwhile. Establish which drivers are affected, then decide with the owner where the mode is latched (at admission of the coordinates request, in the library or in each driver) or whether the mode change is refused while the coordinates are BUSY. Library or generator changes need the owner's approval of the concrete diff.

outcome.summary: Library line, docs and other tests correct. Required: test_mount_lx200_simulator.c check_lx200_sync_result (lx200_sync_result_carries_the_reported_position): the remaining flake is a test weakness. generic/classic/stargo2 profiles publish a phantom slew on the first poll after connect (lastRA/lastDec start at 0, meade_update_generic_state), coordinates BUSY ~0.07-0.7 s; the cached not-BUSY wait cannot see a BUSY set in memory but not yet published. Fix: retry the mode selection when it comes back ALERT (wait for not-BUSY, resend, at most 3 times) or select SYNC only after the first poll published (then wait_for_fresh_coordinates must be restructured). Non-blocking: pre-existing lx200 phantom slew after connect (driver, not fixed here); same cached-state weakness in classic_pulse_refuses; no-op mode re-selection while BUSY also answered with ALERT; sync during GoTo now reports 'Mount is busy, the new coordinates are ignored'; pmc8 and lx200 test files changed without recorded runs.

Round 2 (delta 4bc508705..73b3c042c, test_mount_lx200_simulator.c): lx_select_mode closes the window (the refusal depends only on the in-memory gap between setting BUSY and publishing it, no serial I/O there; 200 ms sleep then cached not-BUSY wait); the revision-based wait cannot pass on a stale publication and is bounded at 10 s; cases still prove what they are named for; formatting clean. Reviewer ran classic-guiding case 1x and sync-result case 2x, PASS; retry branch verified by reading. Non-blocking: find_cached_property(...)->state without NULL check matches existing style.

history.text: Implementation started on branch ticket/d0a643e1-4b83-4dc7-af8e-eb8fee0056c5

Proposed fix, library change needing the owner's approval of the concrete diff: in indigo_mount_change_property() (indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c, MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET branch) add before the copy: INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF(MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES_PROPERTY->state == INDIGO_BUSY_STATE, MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET_PROPERTY, "Mount is busy, the mode is not changed"); so the mode cannot change between the admission of a coordinates request (which sets BUSY) and the end of the operation. One place for all drivers, no driver reads change. agent_mount and agent_alpaca set the mode before the request and already refuse to act on a busy mount. Risk: a client that restores the mode right after sending a sync or GoTo, while the coordinates are still BUSY, gets ALERT and the mode stays. Alternative: latch the mode at admission in every driver (about 12 drivers, each with a version bump and a recorded run). Approve the library diff?

Owner 2026-11-22: 'Yes, in the library' - approved the library diff: in the MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET branch of indigo_mount_change_property() add INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF(MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES_PROPERTY->state == INDIGO_BUSY_STATE, MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET_PROPERTY, "Mount is busy, the mode is not changed"); before the copy. No per-driver latching.

Review changes (lx200 test only), wip 73b3c042c. Cause found by the reviewer: for the generic, classic and stargo2 profiles the first poll after connect reports a phantom slew (meade_update_generic_state(), driver:3494, lastRA/lastDec start at 0 while the simulator starts at RA 6h), so the coordinates go OK -> BUSY (~0.07-0.11 s) -> OK (~0.7 s); the poll sets BUSY in memory (driver:3761) before publishing it at the end of on_timer (driver:3836), so a cached not-BUSY wait cannot see it and the mode selection is refused. Fix in test_mount_lx200_simulator.c: helper lx_select_mode() waits until the cached coordinates are not BUSY, selects the mode and, when the answer is ALERT, waits 200 ms and repeats, at most 3 times; it prints the states only on final failure (the earlier diagnostic line was removed). Used in check_lx200_sync_result(), classic_pulse_refuses() and the accepted-GoTo step of lx200_classic_guiding_refusal_is_published. check_lx200_sync_result() now takes the OK-publication revision before the selection, so the first poll's publication still counts when a retried selection has waited for it (wait_for_fresh_coordinates() taken after the selection would miss it). Verification under the lock: lx200_sync_result_carries_the_reported_position 40/40 (one run went through the retry and passed, counted with a temporary marker since removed), lx200_classic_guiding_refusal_is_published 15/15, then one full run_driver_test.py mount_lx200 --no-record 169/169 OK. flow check passed on 73b3c042c. notes.text:
Implementation (base c3c8b8e53, wip dc6164cb9).

LIBRARY (owner-approved line only), indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c, indigo_mount_change_property(), MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET branch, before the copy:
  INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF(MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES_PROPERTY->state == INDIGO_BUSY_STATE, MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET_PROPERTY, "Mount is busy, the mode is not changed");
MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET is never BUSY, so indigo_reject_change() forces every item and publishes ALERT with the message (the client rolls back to the kept mode); the next accepted change copies and publishes OK (covered by a case). Docs: one sentence each in indigo_mount_driver.h (MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET doc comment), PROPERTIES.md (MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET row) and DRIVER_DEVELOPMENT_BASICS.md (selector paragraph, with the condition that the coordinates stay BUSY until the handler's last read of the mode). No generator change, no driver change, no driver version bump.

AUDIT (handlers and finalizers run on the device queue under the device mutex; change_property runs on the bus thread under the bus mutex, so the guard holds exactly while the in-memory state of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES is BUSY):
| driver | BUSY at admission | where the mode is read | guard covers it |
| mount_ioptron | yes (COPY_TARGETS macro) | handler only, after on_change sets BUSY again, no OK prologue | yes |
| mount_lx200 | yes | handler: generated OK prologue (c:4835), BUSY again at c:4841 before the reads (c:4845/4859); window of a few instructions, no I/O | yes, except a microsecond window |
| mount_nexstar | yes | handler: generated OK prologue (c:1131), then nexstar_set_coordinates() does serial I/O (tc_check_align) before reading the mode (c:647), sends goto or sync, reads again (c:650/653) and once more after return (c:1135, driver:895) | NO: the in-memory state is OK during the serial transactions; a mode change in that window is accepted, e.g. a goto sent (TRACK at 647) and then treated as a sync at 1135 (property OK, position read back, goto_active set only if TRACK still on at 653) |
| mount_nexstaraux | yes | handler only, on_change sets BUSY, no prologue; slew finalizer does not read the mode | yes |
| mount_pmc8 | yes | handler only, no prologue (stop tracking + 200 ms sleep happen while BUSY) | yes |
| mount_rainbow | yes | handler (no prologue) and change_property guard (sync check on bus thread at admission) | yes |
| mount_simulator | yes | handler: generated OK prologue (c:433) immediately followed by the reads (c:435-451), no I/O | yes, except a microsecond window between the prologue and the reads |
| mount_starbook | yes | handler, latched into a local before I/O, no prologue | yes |
| mount_synscan | yes; sync_pending latched in on_change_request at admission | handler uses the latch; GoTo finalizer reads TRACK at the end of the slew (c:2109, driver:2041) while the coordinates are still BUSY (state published later by synscan_update_mount_coordinates()) | yes |
| mount_temma | yes | handler only, before and after serial I/O, no prologue; start/stop tracking latched into private data for the poll | yes |
| system_alpaca mount | yes (system_alpaca_accept() sets BUSY under its lock, ANYTIME accept refuses BUSY via mount_coordinates_refusal) | handler (c:993/1000/1018), also when re-run after a settle/unpark postponement (coordinates stay BUSY meanwhile); MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET falls through to indigo_mount_change_property() | yes |
| mount_asi (off limits, read only) | NO: copy_targets at admission, BUSY set only in mount_eq_coords_callback ("Update to busy moved to callback") | callback, after it sets BUSY | NO for admission -> callback start: the ticket's scenario still turns a GoTo into a sync |
| mount_mxhd (off limits, read only) | NO: copy_targets at admission | callback reads SYNC/SLEW (c:1075/1088) before it sets BUSY (c:1103), after motor-recovery serial I/O | NO for admission -> c:1103 |
| system_ascol (off limits, read only) | n/a: handled synchronously in change_property | never reads the mode (only TRACK item, count 1) | not affected |
All drivers route MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET to indigo_mount_change_property() (none handles it itself), so the guard applies to all of them whenever the coordinates are BUSY. No linux/mac/optional driver handles MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES. Not covered and not fixed here (driver work, not in scope): mount_nexstar (generated OK prologue before serial I/O; fix in the .driver: keep BUSY until the reads, e.g. read the mode once at the top), mount_asi and mount_mxhd (no BUSY at admission; off limits). mount_simulator and mount_lx200 keep a race window of a few instructions after the generated OK prologue; not reproducible by a test. The approved line is therefore not enough for nexstar, asi and mxhd; the library change was not extended.
mount_synscan: the GoTo finalizer read of TRACK is covered by the library guard and by this audit, not by a synscan case (the synscan suite is being changed by two other tickets).

CLIENTS
- agent_mount (mount_dome_control, c:394): sets the mode then the coordinates; every entry point refuses while the cached mount coordinates are BUSY (START_PROCESS guard c:2351, LX200 :MS/:CM c:954/968), never restores the mode afterwards. Not broken. Its simulator case sync_refused_by_a_foreign_slew_is_reported_failed switches to TRACK before the foreign GoTo is admitted, unaffected.
- agent_alpaca (c:571-739): sets TRACK/SYNC then coordinates; sync paths refuse while its cached slewing flag is set; slew paths do not, so a slew requested during a slew now also gets MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET ALERT (value unchanged), while the coordinates are refused by the existing BUSY guard exactly as before; canslew/cansync come from item presence, not state. Not broken.
- agent_scripting Sequencer.js writes only DOME_ON_COORDINATES_SET; no other writer in agents, indigo_libs, indigo_tools, indigo_server or *.js. agent_astrometry/platesolver do not write the mode (their test sets it while idle).
- Residual, by design of the two-request protocol: a client that sends mode + coordinates while a slew is just ending can have the mode refused and the coordinates accepted with the previous mode (before the change the opposite race was the ticket's bug). Clients should check the MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET answer; both agents send only while the mount is not BUSY.

TESTS (indigo_test/integration/test_mount_simulator.c, new self-contained functions after mount_sync_during_goto_is_refused_with_busy_message):
- mount_mode_change_during_goto_is_refused: (a)+(c) mode change during a BUSY GoTo -> ALERT, message "Mount is busy, the mode is not changed", items keep TRACK, GoTo ends OK at its target, no alignment point (NEAREST_POINT), then SYNC and TRACK accepted with OK.
- mount_mode_switch_behind_queued_goto_keeps_the_goto: (b) gate holds the device queue, GoTo admitted, SYNC requested before the handler runs, gate released -> slew light BUSY, mount moves to the target, no alignment point, mode TRACK, property ALERT with the message.
- mount_mode_change_while_coordinates_idle_or_alert_is_accepted: (d) coordinates kept ALERT (parked refusal) and idle after a sync -> mode changes accepted with OK, coordinates keep their state, no ALERT.
- Adapted existing case mount_sync_during_goto_is_refused_with_busy_message (obsolete expectation): it switched to SYNC during the GoTo and waited for OK, then expected "Sync refused, the mount is busy"; now the switch is refused (ALERT), the coordinates are refused as a GoTo with "Mount is busy, the new coordinates are ignored", and the second GoTo is sent without re-selecting TRACK (re-selecting is refused too). The rest of the case is unchanged.
Before/after (same binary, libindigo.dylib built without/with the line):
- without the line: mount_mode_change_during_goto_is_refused FAIL (line 1819, MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET OK instead of ALERT); mount_mode_switch_behind_queued_goto_keeps_the_goto FAIL (slew light never BUSY: the handler synced, the mount did not move); idle/alert case PASS; adapted case FAIL (switch accepted instead of refused).
- with the line: all four PASS.
Repetitions: new + adapted cases 10x each (20 binary runs, 40 case runs), 0 failures.

questions.text: Proposed fix, library change needing the owner's approval of the concrete diff: in indigo_mount_change_property() (indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c, MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET branch) add before the copy: INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF(MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES_PROPERTY->state == INDIGO_BUSY_STATE, MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET_PROPERTY, "Mount is busy, the mode is not changed"); so the mode cannot change between the admission of a coordinates request (which sets BUSY) and the end of the operation. One place for all drivers, no driver reads change. agent_mount and agent_alpaca set the mode before the request and already refuse to act on a busy mount. Risk: a client that restores the mode right after sending a sync or GoTo, while the coordinates are still BUSY, gets ALERT and the mode stays. Alternative: latch the mode at admission in every driver (about 12 drivers, each with a version bump and a recorded run). Approve the library diff?
questions.answer: Owner 2026-11-22: 'Yes, in the library' - approved the library diff: in the MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET branch of indigo_mount_change_property() add INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF(MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES_PROPERTY->state == INDIGO_BUSY_STATE, MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET_PROPERTY, "Mount is busy, the mode is not changed"); before the copy. No per-driver latching.
